answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a node’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster isolated by a sparse external cut has low conductance; under bounded-degree and honest-seed assumptions, min-cut transitivity bounds limit how much voting mass can cross that boundary. Even a walnut-sized haven cannot amplify its pulse of coordinated attestations beyond the cut’s constrained flow.
